vnode.ui:help: Optional: Group metrics under a virtual node for multi-instance setups.

timeout.ui:help: Accepts decimals for sub-second granularity (e.g., 0.5 for 500ms).

mode.ui:help:
Choose how Netdata gets Azure credentials.

- `service_principal`: Use an Azure app / service principal. Requires `tenant_id`, `client_id`, and `client_secret` in `mode_service_principal`.
- `managed_identity`: Use the managed identity attached to the Azure resource running Netdata. Set `mode_managed_identity.client_id` only for a user-assigned identity.
- `default`: Use the Azure SDK `DefaultAzureCredential` chain. This automatically tries available Azure credential sources, such as environment-based credentials, managed identity, and local developer credentials.

Use `service_principal` for explicit app credentials. Use `managed_identity` when Netdata runs on an Azure resource with an attached identity. Use `default` when you want Azure SDK auto-discovery or local development convenience.

disabled.ui:help: WARNING: Query Store may contain unmasked PII (customer names, emails, IDs) in query text. Query text and runtime views require version-specific server and per-database performance-state permissions.

time_window_days.ui:help: Limits Query Store data to recent days. Lower positive values improve performance on busy servers; 0 uses 7 days and -1 includes all available history.

disabled.ui:help: WARNING: Query text may contain unmasked sensitive literals. Requires VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE on SQL Server 2022+, or VIEW SERVER STATE on older versions. Unavailable on Azure SQL Database.

use_ring_buffer.ui:help: Use the volatile system_health ring buffer on SQL Server or Azure SQL Managed Instance. It can be slower to parse. Azure SQL Database is unsupported.

disabled.ui:help: WARNING: Error messages and query text may contain unmasked sensitive literals. Requires VIEW SERVER PERFORMANCE STATE on SQL Server 2022+, VIEW SERVER STATE on older versions, or on Azure SQL Database VIEW DATABASE PERFORMANCE STATE for event_file and VIEW DATABASE STATE for ring_buffer.

session_name.ui:help: The administrator-created Extended Events session must capture sqlserver.error_reported with sql_text and query_hash actions, using an event_file (default) or ring_buffer target. Use ON DATABASE for Azure SQL Database.

use_ring_buffer.ui:help: Use the volatile ring buffer when persistent event_file storage is unavailable. The session must remain running and XML parsing can be slower.
